correctness.rationale: The centered cube projection is centrally symmetric; hence its minimum enclosing disk is centered at zero and maximization over the eight projected vertices gives R²=3-min_j(v_j·U)² for four antipodal tetrahedral axes. Their tight-frame identity gives support [sqrt(2),sqrt(3)]. Each axis defines a belt of probability t/sqrt(3); conditioning on one latitude gives the stated arcsine integral J(t) for each of six equal belt pairs. Inversion of any three rows gives 1=||U||²=[(q+h)²+(p-h)²+(p-q)²]/4<=3t², excluding positive-area triple intersections for 0<t<=1/sqrt(3); an explicit normal produces triple overlap above. Therefore inclusion-exclusion gives 4t/sqrt(3)-6J(t), exactly on the claimed interval. Taylor expansion of the joint two-axis density and t²=2sqrt(3)epsilon-epsilon² verifies coefficients, including the negative linear epsilon correction. Independent random-sphere 500,000-normal checks at three thresholds agree with analytic quadrature (not proof of continuity). The lower-radius distribution is unproved.
